sampling_model.design: Uniformly draw an ordered tuple of \(G_n\) pairwise-disjoint \(M\)-subsets of \(\mathcal U_n\), then independently and completely randomize exactly \(G_{1n}\) group labels to treatment.
sampling_model.units: The \(n\) labeled units and every composition-indexed potential outcome are fixed; assignment is the only randomness.
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment is shared within each realized group, with \(p_n=G_{1n}/G_n\to p\in(0,1)\).
sampling_model.overlap: The grouped-unit fraction satisfies \(N_n/n\to\rho\in[0,1]\); no birthday-scale condition on \(N_n^2/n\) is imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no superpopulation nuisances. The latent object affecting exact variance is \(E_{\tau,1,n}\), the degree-one Johnson energy of the arm difference.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 cover a fixed finite menu of admissible group sizes under \(N_n^2/n\to0\) and their Assumption 1; the present homogeneous \(K=1\) result replaces those premises by sampling-fraction, nondegeneracy, and predictable-variation conditions, so the comparison is an assumption trade rather than a pure weakening.
Theorem 3 and the Johnson-scheme discussion provide an orthogonal harmonic basis and common eigenspaces for functions on a slice.
Proposition 3.1 records the classical eigenvalues for distance graphs in the Johnson scheme, including the Kneser relation.
Theorems 3--4 establish finite-population Gaussian limits for complete randomization on fixed experimental units.
Theorem 1 makes CR2 exactly unbiased under a specified independent-cluster working covariance model.
Theorem 1 relates regression sandwich estimators to conservative Neyman variances when clusters are fixed.
The paper characterizes optimized estimable conservative quadratic variance bounds under interference and complex designs because exact variance is generally unavailable.
Theorems 1--2 show that design-unbiased estimators can fail to concentrate under arbitrary or network interference.

body.tldr:
For fixed group size \(M\), the exact Kneser decomposition gives
\[
G_n\sigma_n^2
=R_n-\frac{N_n}{n-M}E_{\tau,1,n}+O(n^{-1}),
\]
uniformly over bounded composition-interference schedules.  The equal-group CR2 statistic obeys the matching expansion with remainder \(O_{\mathbb P}(G_n^{-1/2}+n^{-1})\), revealing a bias-versus-noise elbow at \(N_n\asymp n^{2/3}\) when \(E_{\tau,1,n}\to e>0\).  A unit-permutation-then-label-permutation martingale gives pointwise centered Gaussian inference under the stated predictable-quadratic-variation condition; for \(N_n/n\to0\), CR2 studentization is valid without \(N_n^2/n\to0\), while for positive limiting density it is conservative and ratio-consistent exactly when the projection correction is negligible.  The exact \(n=8\) witness has variance \(1/7\) and expected CR2 variance \(2/7\).  Finally, the Rademacher predictable-variation calculation and diagonal argument prove that no one-realization estimator is uniformly ratio-consistent for the exact variance.  That lower bound already holds on the additive no-interference subclass and therefore transfers to arbitrary composition interference.  The positive theory remains homogeneous in group size and does not transfer automatically to variable-size designs.

project_justification.gap: \cite{FuSamiiWang2026}, Theorems 1--2, cover a fixed finite menu of admissible group sizes and use \(N_n^2/n\to0\) together with their Assumption 1 to transport an independent-group limit.  This note studies their exact homogeneous \(K=1\) design and PAME subcase, but replaces those conditions by a sampling-fraction regime, scaled-variance nondegeneracy, and statistic-specific predictable-quadratic-variation stabilization.  The beyond-birthday conclusion is therefore an assumption trade, not a pure weakening.  Whole-tuple coupling also removes the first-order finite-pool dependence that survives when \(N_n/n\) is nonnegligible, and the cited cluster-robust literature does not recover that projection correction or the corresponding impossibility of uniformly exact one-realization variance estimation.
project_justification.niche: For the fixed-\(M\) homogeneous design, disjointness is the normalized Kneser operator on the uniform slice.  Diagonalizing that operator before averaging over complete treatment randomization isolates the unique degree-one memory of finite-pool competition, supplies a uniform finite-\(n\) remainder, and links the dense variance correction to both CR2's conservative phase and the equal-observation lower-bound construction.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the exact finite-sample covariance and PAME variance identities, sharpens the scaled variance to a uniform \(O(n^{-1})\) remainder, obtains the CR2 comparison at rate \(O_{\mathbb P}(G_n^{-1/2}+n^{-1})\), and exposes the \(N_n\asymp n^{2/3}\) mesoscopic elbow.  It proves a pointwise centered martingale CLT under explicit predictable-variation stabilization, the resulting Wald and CR2 phase statements, the exact equal-group \({\tt clubSandwich::vcovCR}\) consumer, and the eight-unit factor-two witness.  It also proves the all-statistic lower bound by verifying predictable variation for two additive Rademacher priors and selecting deterministic schedule arrays from their high-probability supports.

body.related_work: \cite{FuSamiiWang2026} is the closest theorem-level comparator.  Its Theorems 1--2 treat a fixed finite menu of admissible group sizes under \(N_n^2/n\to0\) and its Assumption 1.  The present design and PAME are their exact homogeneous \(K=1\) subcase, but the inference classes are incomparable as stated: sampling-fraction asymptotics, scaled-variance nondegeneracy, and predictable-quadratic-variation stabilization replace their birthday condition and Assumption 1.  Thus the sparse result is a statistic-specific assumption trade, not a pure weakening; conversely, this note's positive homogeneous results do not establish the variable-size case.  Theorem 1 and the Johnson-scheme discussion of \cite{Filmus2016}, together with Proposition 3.1 of \cite{BrouwerEtAl2018}, supply the classical eigenspace and Kneser-spectrum substrate, while the causal variance propagation and uniform remainder are derived here.  The complete-randomization comparison in \cite{LiDing2017} and the sampling martingale in \cite{Ohlsson1989} inform the two reveal phases but do not cover a positive-fraction random partition with composition-indexed outcomes.  \cite{PustejovskyTipton2018} and \cite{SuDing2021} concern independent or fixed clusters and therefore do not insert the finite-pool projection correction into CR2.  \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026} studies optimized estimable conservative quadratic bounds, and \cite{BasseAiroldi2018} gives broader interference nonconcentration results; neither supplies the equal-observation additive Rademacher pair, its filtration-specific predictable-variation calculation, or the separated dense PAME variance constants used by the present uniform lower bound.  The lower bound is proved on the additive no-interference subclass, so it applies a fortiori to the encompassing arbitrary composition-interference class.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The deterministic \(O(n^{-1})\) remainder uses fixed \(M\), uniform boundedness, and treatment fractions bounded away from zero; the pointwise CLT additionally uses scaled-variance nondegeneracy and the stated predictable-quadratic-variation stabilization.  The latter is verified for the Rademacher prior rows used in the impossibility proof, but it is not claimed to follow automatically for every bounded composition-interference schedule.  CR2 need not be conservative at finite \(n\), because the higher Johnson eigenvalues alternate in sign; the theorem gives asymptotic conservativeness.  The impossibility result requires \(\rho>0\), concerns uniform ratio consistency for the exact variance from one realization, and does not preclude pointwise recovery on structural subclasses, repeated regrouping, or estimable conservative bounds.  It transfers upward from additive no interference to arbitrary composition interference, whereas none of the positive fixed-size arguments transfers without new work to a variable group-size menu.
body.honest_scope:
The design uniformly selects \(G_n\) disjoint groups of one fixed size \(M\), then completely randomizes exactly \(G_{1n}\) group labels; the potential-outcome array is fixed and assignment is the only randomness.  The exact Kneser and design-variance identities hold finitely, and bounded schedules give the uniform expansions
\[
G_n\sigma_n^2=R_n-\frac{N_n}{n-M}E_{\tau,1,n}+O(n^{-1})
\]
and
\[
G_n(\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}-\sigma_n^2)
=\frac{N_n}{n-M}E_{\tau,1,n}
+O_{\mathbb P}(G_n^{-1/2}+n^{-1}).
\]
Centered Gaussian inference is pointwise over deterministic arrays satisfying the explicit predictable-variation condition; it is not asserted uniformly over every bounded schedule.  At \(\rho=0\), the result permits \(N_n^2/n\to\infty\), but this substitutes statistic-specific martingale regularity for the conditions in \cite{FuSamiiWang2026}.  At \(\rho>0\), CR2 is asymptotically conservative and becomes ratio-consistent exactly when the projection correction is negligible; no finite-sample conservativeness claim is made.  The one-realization exact-variance lower bound is complete for the full dense class because it holds on its additive no-interference subclass, with the filtration condition verified and deterministic supports obtained by diagonal selection.  The positive results are restricted to homogeneous fixed-size groups and make no claim for the variable-size designs also allowed by \cite{FuSamiiWang2026}.
